- Where this brief and the VISUAL STORY PLAN disagree on the figure's shape, this brief wins. The figure itself is drawn by the archetype component library under the contract below; the server rejects a slide that departs from it.
FIGURE CONTRACT (the figure below is finished markup; reproduce it, do not redesign it):
1. Paste the following figure into the slide body EXACTLY as given — every element, class, data-qid, data-native, data-qid-ignore and text — at the place your layout reserves for it. This archetype has an intrinsic height ceiling: give its container an explicit width and a height of exactly 320px — the honest maximum a gauge figure reaches at this node count without padding itself with blank interior space. Do NOT stretch it toward y=648px or down to the 430px floor that applies to other archetypes: an inflated figure is the same defect as a blank band, just moved inside the box instead of under it. Spend the rest of the content area, down to y=648px, one of two ways: (a) place a text column of its own BESIDE the figure so the two together — the figure in the wider column — fill the full content width and reach the bottom line; or (b), when this slide has nothing more to say, centre the figure vertically in the content area with the takeaway above it, leaving the remaining space as plain margin — never as an invented caption or a spacer manufactured to fill it. The figure fills the box you give it: put no width, height, margin or position on the figure's own root element — the library sizes the root to 100% of its container, so a margin on the root pushes the figure past the canvas edge.
2. The figure's stylesheet is injected by the server. Do NOT write CSS for any .ig* class, do NOT add a class the library does not define, and do NOT put a style attribute or a <style> element inside the figure (the only exception: left/top on .ig-co / .ig-pin, kept in the percentages the skeleton gives, and the px size of a scene img).
3. You MAY: swap any icon inside an .ig-ic for another from the ICON MENU; rewrite the UPPERCASE placeholder words in the deck language; and do what the ARCHETYPE NOTE allows. Every other text is verbatim from the plan — never reword, translate, add or drop a label.
4. Everything outside the figure (header, eyebrow, page number, any supporting text) is yours to author under the design system as usual, but no other diagram, card grid or chart may compete with the figure.
ARCHETYPE NOTE (gauge): Pick the dial class v10..v100 on .ig-dial-ring that matches the first node's share (v70 for 72%). The other nodes are the facts beside the dial.
